stem: Before dispensing Xyrem, a pharmacist reviews both controlled-substance and product-specific obligations. Select all supported conclusions.

choices.text: Current product-specific REMS requirements must be satisfied.
REMS enrollment converts the drug to Schedule VI.
Federal Schedule III refill limits remain independently applicable.
REMS replaces every controlled-substance record requirement.
A Medication Guide can be omitted whenever a REMS exists.

explanation.core_reasoning: Apply each proposition independently. A pharmacy dispensing a drug subject to an FDA REMS must follow the current product-specific certification, authorization, documentation, and safe-use requirements that apply to the dispenser. A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner. sodium oxybate (Xyrem) is used for treatment of cataplexy or excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy. It is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.

choice_analysis.A: The proposition 'Current product-specific REMS requirements must be satisfied.' is supported by Product-specific FDA REMS requirements: A pharmacy dispensing a drug subject to an FDA REMS must follow the current product-specific certification, authorization, documentation, and safe-use requirements that apply to the dispenser.
choice_analysis.B: This statement imports Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.C: The proposition 'Federal Schedule III refill limits remain independently applicable.' is supported by Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits: A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
choice_analysis.D: This statement imports Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.E: This statement imports Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
